stories.title: Taoiseach in Kyiv to pledge EU support in war effort
stories.summary: Taoiseach Micheál Martin is in Kyiv today for a bilateral meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. The two leaders are expected to discuss Russia's ongoing war of aggression against Ukraine and European Union support for the country during Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the European Union, including Ukraine’s accession negotiations. The Taoiseach will also meet with Ukraine’s new Prime Minister, Serhii Koretskyi, who was appointed last week. Mr Martin will then visit the Ukrainian parliament (Verkhovna Rada) and meet its speaker Ruslan Stefanchuk. They are to discuss Ukraine’s EU accession negotiations and the agenda for domestic reforms, which Ukraine needs to implement in order to join the bloc.

stories.title: Deep clean at Offaly garda station after vape incident
stories.summary: A specialist deep clean is due to take place today at a Co Offaly garda station following an incident with seized vapes that resulted in two gardaí being hospitalised. Gardaí said that the two men in Edenderry Garda Station became unwell when they were involved in processing vape products. These products were seized from a commercial premises during a recent investigation. Both male members were taken to hospital, where they remain under medical assessment.

stories.title: Houthis claim Red Sea tanker strikes, US hits Iran again
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels have claimed military strikes on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, potentially opening a new front in the US-Iran war engulfing the region. The rebels' claim came as the United States launched a fresh wave of strikes on Iranian military targets, marking the twelfth consecutive night of US attacks on Iran. The Houthis said they had carried out missile and drone strikes on two Saudi tankers that "violated the blockade", naming the vessels as the Encelia and the Layla. British naval security monitor UKMTO said the master of a tanker reported being struck by an unknown projectile about 70 nautical miles southwest of Al Shuqaiq, causing a fire that the crew was fighting.

stories.title: 'Too early' to assess forest fire damage in Tipperary
stories.summary: It is "too early" to assess the damage to a forest in Co Tipperary following a major wildfire burning on Slievenamon, a Coillte official has said. The fire spread yesterday to a forestry plantation on the mountain and fire and rescue services are focusing their efforts on that area to stop the blaze spreading further. Pat Neville, Communications Manager at Coillte, said that last night, the fire "progressed significantly through the forest ... despite the best efforts of crews on the ground and supported by a helicopter". He said the "immediate focus" alongside Tipperary fire service and emergency responders is to contain the fire "as quickly and as safely as possible".

stories.title: Weight loss drugs 'linked to hair loss' - study
stories.summary: Weight loss and diabetes drugs like Mounjaro, Ozempic and Wegovy are linked to an increased risk of hair loss, according to researchers. People on GLP-1 agonist drugs have been reporting hair loss to regulators, but a new study on around 50,000 people appears to firm up the link. Experts used electronic patient data from the University of Pennsylvania Health System to compare rates of alopecia hair loss in adults using GLP-1s to manage diabetes with those on other drugs. The team noted that regulators in the US have been informed of the link between the drugs and hair loss, particularly for semaglutide (Wegovy and Ozempic) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro).

stories.title: Ex-minister sent letter of concern over Bessborough site
stories.summary: A submission to An Coimisiún Pleanála by former minister for children Katherine Zappone raised serious concerns over the mother and baby home site at Bessborough in Cork, according to the Special Advocate for survivors of institutional abuse. Ms Zappone’s letter was included in the collection of publicly available submissions to An Coimisiún Pleanála obtained by the Special Advocate’s office. Two weeks ago, An Coimisiún Pleanála upheld planning permission for a 106-apartment development on the former Bessborough Mother and Baby Home site in Cork. In correspondence, Ms Zappone, who, as minister for children held responsibility for the oversight of the Mother and Baby Home Commission (2016-2020), made a number of observations, including that "enough was not done to determine burial sites" at Bessborough.

stories.title: €10m in funding announced for NI reconciliation projects
stories.summary: The Minister for Foreign Affairs has announced funding of almost €10 million for 154 peacebuilding and reconciliation projects across Northern Ireland. It is the first round of allocations under a new three-year Reconciliation Fund Strategy (2026-2029). Helen McEntee said the funding was an investment in community organisations that help maintain stability and referenced their role during recent disorder in Belfast, where some groups worked to reduce tensions, support displaced migrant families and keep young people away from violence. There is also an emphasis on organisations that combat violence against women and girls, with 11 organisations receiving funding for projects addressing domestic, sexual and gender-based violence.

stories.title: EU agrees new round of sanctions on Russia - diplomats
stories.summary: European Union countries have agreed a new watered-down round of sanctions on Russia over the Ukraine war after weeks of haggling, diplomats said, freezing the level of an oil price cap. The package - the 21st by the EU since Moscow's 2022 invasion - was held up by a raft of objections by member states to various proposed elements. The technical work on the sanctions package ‌will now be concluded, and ‌a written procedure for adoption will ‌be launched this afternoon, according to a diplomat. Pleased we have agreed the 21st package of sanctions in the first weeks of the 🇮🇪Presidency. This package further targets Russia's revenue streams, impedes its shadow fleet and disrupts its supply-chains. Europe stands with Ukraine against Russia's brutal war of aggression
